dedupe_keys.name: saarc energy data portal energy indicators power plants trade flows and policies for south asia

description: The SAARC Energy Centre, set up in Islamabad in 2006 under the 2005 Dhaka Declaration to work towards a South Asian energy ring, runs the SAARC Energy Data Portal, a web application backed by a public JSON API. The API's indicator list read today holds 87 indicators in seven groups: socioeconomic data, energy data (primary supply, reserves, production, installed capacity, electricity production, self-sufficiency and final consumption), renewable energy, energy access (SDG 7 electricity and clean cooking), efficiency and losses, electricity and fuel prices, and environmental data. The portal also has an infrastructure section of power plants classed by 12 fuel or technology types (hydel, coal, gas, RLNG, nuclear, wind, solar, bagasse and oil products such as HSD and RFO), trade flows for oil and oil products, coal, natural gas and electricity, a policy database with categories and a timeline, an experts directory and a SAARC energy data book (PDF). Its country list covers Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, plus Myanmar. The Centre's site also keeps an information database of literature on cross-border electricity trade. Coverage: South Asia. Format and access: web portal and JSON API; free. Licence: not read. Caveats: indicator values, years and the power plant records themselves were not read, only the lists of indicators, plant types, trade categories and countries. Simulation uses: national capacity, generation, losses and cross-border energy trade for South Asian power system and interconnection studies. Related records: the APEC Energy Database (data-apec-egeda-energy-database) covers the Asia-Pacific economies.
